issues.description: Element: Milkable.messageOnMilk(...). The problem statement contains two conflicting specifications for this method: the UML/interface diagram (problem_statement.md) and the template/solution code declare a parameterless method 'String messageOnMilk()'; however the Part 2 textual instructions (problem_statement.md) describe a parameterized signature 'messageOnMilk(double milkVolume)' and require a return string containing the volume. This inconsistency leaves students uncertain which method signature to implement and what the expected return format is (with or without volume), and can cause compilation or test mismatches if they follow the wrong artifact.
issues.suggestedFix: Pick one consistent signature and update all artifacts to match. Option A (preferred if volume tracking is required): change the UML, template code, and solution to declare 'String messageOnMilk(double milkVolume)' and update all implementations (Seal, Goat, etc.), calls (e.g., in Main and tests), and example return formats to include the volume '(volume: [milkVolume]L)'. Option B (preferred if no volume is intended): update the Part 2 textual description to specify 'String messageOnMilk()' with no parameters and remove any '(volume: ...L)' wording so it matches the UML, template, and solution. Ensure the problem statement, template code, and solution/tests all consistently use the chosen signature.

issues.description: The concept is 'milking an animal'. The problem statement's Part 2 text requires a method named messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (a method that accepts a double and whose example return string includes the volume). However, the UML in the problem (messageOnMilk():String), the template usage in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java (call to m.messageOnMilk()), and the solution's Milkable interface (String messageOnMilk();) all declare/use a no-argument method messageOnMilk(). This creates an inconsistent API across artifacts: the textual requirement asks for messageOnMilk(double), while the provided template and solution expect messageOnMilk() with no parameter. Students will be unsure which signature to implement and which one will be used by the tests and example code, causing confusion and blocking progress.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnMilk API consistent across all artifacts. Preferred, low-friction fix: update the problem statement text (Part 2) to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and change the example return string to omit the milkVolume (e.g., use "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Alternatively, if including volume is desired pedagogically, change the template and solution to declare messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update all implementations and calls (e.g., Main.java and the UML) to pass a double, and update example return strings to include the formatted volume. Recommendation: apply the first option (update the problem text) since the template and solution currently use the no-argument signature.
